title: C.J. Stroud, Texans pause contract extension negotiations until after season: Source
content:
The Houston Texans and quarterback C.J. Stroud are pausing negotiations around a long-term contract until after the season, a league source told The Athletic. The source spoke on condition of anonymity because discussions are ongoing.

Stroud, 24, will play the 2026 season on the four-year, $36.28 million rookie deal he signed when the Texans drafted him with the second pick in 2023. The Texans exercised his $25.9 million fifth-year option for 2027 in April.

Texans general manager Nick Caserio said at a news conference earlier this month that even though he and Stroud had “productive talks,” negotiations would likely be pushed to next offseason if they couldn’t agree to a new deal before the season began. The Texans open their season against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday.

This season has major implications for Stroud, who sees a long-term future in Houston as the Texans hope to get over the divisional-round playoff hump. Stroud had a promising rookie season in 2023 that earned him Offensive Rookie of the Year honors and a Pro Bowl selection.

During that season, Stroud ranked sixth in expected points added per dropback, per TruMedia, and the Texans advanced to the playoffs for the first time since 2019. He passed for 4,108 yards and 23 touchdowns against five interceptions. Since then, however, his production has dropped.

The former Ohio State passer threw for the fewest yards in his career last season, finishing with 3,041 yards, 19 touchdowns and eight interceptions. He also missed three games with a concussion. And over the Texans’ two playoff games last season, Stroud threw only two touchdown passes against five interceptions and took six sacks.

Stroud is guaranteed to remain in Houston through 2027, but if he has another season similar to his rookie year, it could speed up negotiations on his next deal.
